**VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The component implements a functional infinite scroll pattern but lacks the state communication and structural context required for assistive technology users. While mouse users get visual feedback through scrolling, screen reader users receive no indication of loading progress, loaded content volume, or page context. The design is 80% complete: the list semantics are correct, but the dynamic update pattern violates WAI-ARIA APG guidance for live regions and status messages. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: Before reading code, I predicted: 1. Missing `aria-live` region for loading/loaded announcements (dynamic content updates) 2. No `aria-busy` or loading text during API calls 3. Empty scroll sentinel (`observerTarget`) exposed to assistive technology 4. Missing landmark structure (`
`) and heading hierarchy 5. No focus management strategy for newly loaded content Actual findings align with predictions. The component lacks all predicted state communication and structural elements. **Critical Findings** (blocks access): *(None found. The core interaction does not block access entirely, but degrades significantly for AT users.)* **Major Findings** (significantly degrades experience): 1. **Missing loading/loaded state communication to assistive technology** - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:25-30` (`loadMore` updates state silently) and `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:48-61` (JSX renders list without status region) - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages), WAI-ARIA APG Dynamic Content pattern - **Expected Behavior**: A live region should announce `"Loading..."` when `loadMore` begins and `"10 new items loaded"` when complete. `aria-busy="true"` should wrap the list during fetch. - **Fix**: Add a `
` outside the list. Toggle `aria-busy="true"` on the `
    ` during the async call. Announce completion count after state settles. 2. **Scroll sentinel div exposed to assistive technology** - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:58-60` (`
    `) - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users, keyboard-only users - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) - **Expected Behavior**: The sentinel is a non-interactive scroll trigger. It should be hidden from the accessibility tree to prevent empty element announcements if it receives focus. - **Fix**: Add `aria-hidden="true"` and `tabindex="-1"` to the sentinel div. If CSS focuses it, ensure it remains visually hidden or explicitly styled as inert. **Minor Findings** (friction but workaround exists): - **Missing landmark structure and heading hierarchy**: The component renders inside a bare `
    ` with no `
    `, `
    `, or `

    `/`

    ` context. Screen reader users cannot quickly identify the page purpose or jump to content. `src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:48-61`. Fix: Wrap in `
    ` and add a descriptive heading (`

    Infinite Scroll List

    `) above the list. (WCAG 1.3.1, 2.4.1) **Enhancements** (best practice not met): - **No skip navigation**: If this component is used as a full page or large section, keyboard users lack a bypass block. Add a visually-hidden `Skip to list` at the top. (WCAG 2.4.1) - **Missing `aria-label` on list container**: The `
      ` has no accessible name if it's not the only list on the page. Add `aria-label="Product items"` or similar context. (WCAG 1.3.1) **What's Missing** (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions): - **Missing live region for dynamic updates**: No mechanism to announce state changes to AT. Screen reader users will not know when loading finishes or how many items were added. - **Missing `aria-busy` management**: The list remains in a neutral state during async operations, masking the loading phase from assistive technology. - **Missing focus strategy for loaded content**: While infinite scroll intentionally avoids stealing focus, screen reader users reading the bottom of the list will not know when new content appears without a live region announcement. - **Missing error handling for AT**: If the API fails, there is no `aria-live="assertive"` region to announce the failure. Screen reader users would see no change and assume scrolling is broken. **Multi-Perspective Notes**: | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | HIGH | Silent DOM updates, empty sentinel, no landmarks/headings | | Keyboard-only | MEDIUM | Tab order works, but no visual/loading feedback for scroll trigger | | Low vision | LOW | Works at 200% zoom; lack of loading indicator may cause confusion about page state | | Cognitive | HIGH | No loading/loaded feedback → users may think the page froze or scrolling is broken | | Vestibular & motion | LOW | No animations present | | Auditory access | LOW | Not applicable | | Environmental contrast | LOW | Not applicable | **Verdict Justification**: The component passes basic semantic HTML checks (`
        `/`
      • `) but fails the dynamic content design pattern. Automated tests will not flag missing `aria-live` regions or empty sentinels, yet screen reader users lose track of progress and cognitive users experience unexplained page freezes during API calls. The design requires revision to implement WAI-ARIA APG Dynamic Content patterns before shipping. Upgrading to ACCEPT requires: (1) adding a polite live region for loading/loaded announcements, (2) implementing `aria-busy` during fetch, (3) hiding the scroll sentinel from AT, and (4) adding landmark/headling context. **Open Questions (unscored)**: - Does the parent application provide global landmarks/headings that make this component's structural gaps less impactful? If so, note in implementation. - Is there a maximum item count or pagination fallback for users who prefer explicit navigation over infinite scroll? (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order / 3.2.1 On Focus) - How does the component handle network failures? Without error state communication, AT users will experience silent failure. ### A11y Evidence Finding ``` finding_id: missing-live-region-dynamic-content fingerprint: a7f3c9d2e1b4 source: src/components/BuggyInfiniteScroll.jsx:25-61 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages), WAI-ARIA APG Dynamic Content pattern section_508_fpc_context: not in scope severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: screen-reader=HIGH, cognitive=HIGH evidence: JSX renders
          without aria-live wrapper; loadMore() updates state silently reproduction_steps: 1. Mount component 2. Scroll to trigger loadMore 3. Listen via NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver expected_behavior: Screen reader announces "Loading..." then "10 new items loaded" actual_behavior: No announcement; list updates silently in DOM trend: new ```
